date: # --- 2026-09-28, the attention arm's cost, and what the step is actually made of
# RETRACTION. The rows I put here earlier today -
#   ops-with-attention 25858ms, ops-no-attention 3076ms, fused-forward 3098ms
# - are WRONG and are struck. 25858 was measured with three compilers on the
# box (load 7-19), in the dev profile, and with `--eval-every` enabled. The same
# loop arm at the same shape measures ~1.6 s/step on a quiet machine in release.
# A 16x error, in the pessimistic direction, and I repeated it to the owner as
# a fact before checking it. The 3.076 s no-attention figure is wrong the same
# way. Both are gone rather than restated, because I have no clean way to
# reproduce the exact conditions, and "measured under contention" is not a
# measurement.
# WHAT IS CLEAN, from `--timers` on a quiet card, release build, small preset
# (9,195,854 params), batch 8 x seq 512, depth 2, fp32, aux off, --no-engram.
# Step 0, ms, read off the timer line the trainer already prints:
#   arm      total   fwd   bwd    opt
# Three things in that table, and the first is the only reason to keep it:
# 1. THE OPTIMIZER IS 77% OF THE STEP. 8303 of 10809 ms. Not the attention arm
#    - the optimizer, Muon+ Newton-Schulz over 9.2M params. This is where the
#    time is, and until tonight nobody had looked at it, because the attention
#    arm LOOKED like the cost (see the 25858 row above) and every optimisation
#    effort went there. The arm's forward is 61 ms of a 10809 ms step. Even a
#    free attention arm saves 25% of the step, not 16x.
# 2. The batched ops path is a REAL win where it applies and nowhere else:
#    fwd 109 vs 224 ms, and the arm's marginal forward cost 61 vs 176 ms - 2.9x
#    cheaper. The op-level A/B in burn-gdn2 puts it at 4.1-4.8x over three
#    runs, and the differential test agrees with the loop to 9.1e-6 including
#    a hostile case (||L||_inf = 10.97), with identical gradients (2.40e-2
#    both arms, on the f32 finite-difference noise floor).
# 3. ITS BACKWARD IS 19% SLOWER (1824 vs 1538 ms), which is why the whole-step
#    difference is a wash (1627 vs 1695 ms wall-clock). The 4.4x on the arm
#    does not survive contact with the backward. Not yet diagnosed; the
#    Neumann inversion is batched, so the backward through it may be carrying
#    5-D intermediates the loop never materialised.
# A step time is not a claim; it is an instrument reading, and the instrument is
# `--timers` on a quiet card. Quote the config with it or quote nothing.
# VRAM, from the batch ladder, 60 steps each, aux off. Corrects a claim that
# was repeated here and in several docs: "batch 4 OOMs on 16 GB" is true only
# with the JEPA teacher on (a second full forward). With aux off the card takes
# batch 16 in 5908 MiB, 37% of 16 GB. Throughput is flat from batch 8 to 16,
# which is what a launch-bound workload does - a bigger batch buys gradient
# quality here, not speed.
